channel.title: AI · Christopher Laing
channel.description: Christopher Laing is a software executive combining AI and automation experience with commercial leadership.

item.title: The Bitter Lesson Comes for the Factory
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description:
Every year or so, the people most serious about building software with AI settle on a new craft. First it was prompt engineering, then harness engineering, and now it is the agentic factory. Each was necessary in its moment, each delivered real gains to the people who mastered it, and each is falling to the same force: the Bitter Lesson.

What has changed is not the lesson but the speed at which it is taught. Frontier models are now improving quickly enough that the lesson is outpacing even the people most engaged with the state of the art, and nowhere more so than in software.

item.title: High-Code: The Unexpected Path to AI Democratisation
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description: Years ago, I read a blog post called Always Bet on Text that left a lasting impression on me. Not only did it accord with my own experience, but it gave me a good, compact reference frame to think about technology. No recent technology is more suited to this reference frame than Generative AI, for the simple reason that, at its core, modern GenAI is all about text completion.

item.title: On the Economics and Ergonomics of LLMs
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description: For all the millions of words that have been devoted to the capabilities of LLMs, the economics and ergonomics of these systems seem to me to be under-discussed. In much the same way that technology changes - from records to CDs to streaming - have been a dominant factor in the evolution of popular music, prosaic matters such as cost structures will have a substantial influence on the development and impact of AI. While it is still early days for LLMs, there are already signs that economic factors are impacting everything from product design and technology choice to adoption and even regulation.

item.title: The Decomposition of Large Language Models
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description: While many AI systems can be very complex, Large Language Models (LLMs) seem to be refreshingly simple to understand. With their ability to generate human-like text, applications like ChatGPT have captured the popular imagination. However, as compelling an experience as chatbots are, the tradeoffs that they make can lead us to misunderstand LLMs as a whole. In this post, we will explore the idea that the functions of LLMs can be thought of as discrete capabilities, and how different composition of these functions leads to a much wider variety of user experiences.

item.title: The Large Language Model Iceberg
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description: As the capabilities of Artificial Intelligence (AI) continue to evolve, the term “chatbot” has become synonymous with a new era of digital interactions. What was once a seemingly futuristic concept is now an integral part of our everyday lives. However, it is the Machine Learning models underlying them - Large Language Models (LLMs) - that are the true powers in these waters.

item.title: Three Categories of AI
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description: The term “AI” has at least three entirely different meanings in the modern business context, and any particular business leader usually has only one of these meanings in mind when they use the term. Not only is it common for participants in a discussion to have different interpretations of the term “AI”, but most will be unaware that this terminological confusion exists, leaving leaders in both public and private sector organisations poorly equipped to discuss one of the most important technologies of our time.

item.title: If it's not mysterious, it's not AI
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description:
Businesses are deeply confused about what AI is, and they have every right to be. Differences in terminology have plagued the Data-AI-Software landscape for many years, as anyone who has ever looked for a job as a “Data Scientist” will attest. Attempts to demystify the topic either conjure a series of analogies that are then strained to breaking point, or try to delve into the actual technology behind the hype, leaving everyone more confused than they were before.

I will attempt something different: removing the mystery by embracing the mystery.

item.title: The Bitter Lesson Conditions
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description:
The hard truth of AI is that methods that exploit deep, hard-won human knowledge about a particular domain are outperformed by methods that cleverly exploit the increasing power of computation.

I have a modest proposal to distill this fundamental truth into a set of conditions which, when met, will revolutionise a given field.

Lineage #

I do not claim this insight about the fundamental mechanism of progress in AI as original; I have been heavily influenced by Richard Sutton’s powerful essay The Bitter Lesson .
